lede: Photosynthesis is the reaction that builds food out of carbon dioxide and water, using light caught by chlorophyll. Its rate depends on light, carbon dioxide and temperature, and at any moment whichever of those is in shortest supply is the one holding it back.
can: Write the equation and put light and chlorophyll on the arrow.
Name the limiting factor from any point on a rate graph.
Calculate a rate from a change and a time.

text: Photosynthesis: the equation and what slows it down

md: A plant makes its own food out of air, water and sunlight, and everything you eat begins there. The reaction has a fixed recipe and a fixed set of conditions. Turn the light down, cool it, or take the carbon dioxide away and it slows to whatever the scarcest one allows.

explain: Oxygen. It is the gas that comes out, and it is what you collect as bubbles when you test the rate.

md: Read the equation as a story about **energy**. Light lands on **chlorophyll** inside the **chloroplasts**. That light energy is taken in and locked into glucose, which is why photosynthesis is **endothermic** — energy is absorbed, not released. Some of the glucose is converted straight away into **starch**, which is insoluble and so makes a good store: that is why the starch test tells you whether a leaf has been photosynthesising.

prompt: Some of the glucose is changed straight into starch. Why is starch a good store?
explain: Insoluble, so it stays where it is put and does not upset the cell's water balance.

title: Why the two conditions sit on the arrow
md: Light and chlorophyll are not reactants — nothing is used up. Light is the **energy supply** and chlorophyll is where the light is absorbed; neither appears in the products. Writing them on the arrow is the standard way of showing a condition, and it is the reason 'energy' must never go in one of the answer boxes.

prompt: Photosynthesis is described as endothermic. What does that mean here?
options: Light energy is taken in and stored
The reaction needs no energy at all
answer: Light energy is taken in and stored
explain: Endothermic means energy is taken in. Respiration is the exothermic one — it releases the energy again.

title: The symbol equation, for Higher
md:
$6CO_2 + 6H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2$ — light energy and chlorophyll above and below the arrow.
The six at the front of each reactant and of the oxygen; twelve hydrogens in the glucose. March 2026 examiners said candidates got the formulae right but the **numbers were the wrong size or in the wrong place**: the 2 in $CO_2$ is a small subscript *after* the O, the 6 in $6CO_2$ is a full-size number *in front*.

prompt: In the balanced equation $6CO_2 + 6H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_{12}O_6 + \square O_2$, the missing number is
explain: Six oxygen molecules. Count the oxygen atoms: 12 from 6CO₂ plus 6 from 6H₂O is 18; six stay in the glucose, so twelve leave as 6O₂.

text: Limiting factors: reading the graph, not remembering it

md: Three things can hold photosynthesis back: **light intensity**, **carbon dioxide concentration** and **temperature**. Whichever one is in shortest supply sets the rate — that one is the **limiting factor**. Raise it and the rate climbs; raise any of the others and nothing happens until the short one is fixed. That single idea explains every graph CCEA prints here.

prompt: Which factor sets the rate of photosynthesis?
options: whichever one is in shortest supply
the one with the largest value
answer: whichever one is in shortest supply
explain: The one in shortest supply is the limiting factor. Raising any other changes nothing.

md:
Work along the x-axis.
**At 20% light** the two curves sit on top of each other at 12 bubbles per minute. Extra carbon dioxide changes nothing, so **light intensity is the limiting factor** for both.
**Curve A goes flat at 20 bubbles per minute from 40% light.** More light no longer helps, so light is no longer limiting — here it is the **carbon dioxide concentration**, because the curve with more carbon dioxide keeps climbing.
**Curve B goes flat at 32 from 70% light**, where carbon dioxide or temperature takes over.

prompt: Use the graph. At 50% light intensity, the rate on curve B (0.10% CO₂) is _____ bubbles per minute.
explain: Go up from 50% on the x-axis to the solid curve and across to the y-axis: 27. Draw those two construction lines in the exam — the examiner can see them.

title: Summer 2025 B1 Higher Q9(a), March 2026 B1 Higher Q8(c)
md: Asked to describe a trend, candidates wrote what they remembered instead of what the graph showed; the report is blunt that **the trend must be described from the graph itself**. Fewer then explained the trend by linking it to photosynthesis. In March 2026 most could say the rate would be higher in blue light but stopped there — the missing mark was **more light absorbed, so more photosynthesis**. Describe with numbers, then explain with a because.

**Temperature behaves differently.** Light and carbon dioxide give a curve that rises and then flattens. Temperature gives a curve that rises, peaks at an **optimum**, and then **falls** — because the enzymes controlling photosynthesis are denatured above the optimum, and that change is irreversible.

prompt: A pondweed is at 45 °C, above its optimum. The rate of photosynthesis falls. Why?
options: There is less carbon dioxide in the water
The chlorophyll has turned to starch
explain: Above the optimum the enzymes' active sites change shape permanently. Cooling the pondweed down again does not bring the rate back.

md: **Rates.** A rate is always an amount **divided by** the time it took. If a plant releases 27 cm³ of oxygen in 6 minutes, the rate is 27 ÷ 6 = 4.5 cm³ per minute. When the question gives a starting value as well as a finishing value, subtract first — the amount produced is the **change**, not the final reading.

prompt: Dissolved oxygen rises from 8.4 to 21.6 mg/dm³ in 30 minutes. The rate of oxygen production, in mg/dm³ per minute, is
explain: 21.6 − 8.4 = 13.2, then 13.2 ÷ 30 = 0.44. Summer 2024 examiners reported that a large number forgot the subtraction and divided 21.6 by 30 instead.

md:
Write the **word equation** and put light and chlorophyll on the arrow.
Explain why photosynthesis is **endothermic** and where the **starch** comes from.
Name the three **limiting factors** and read one off a graph.
Explain why a temperature curve **falls** past its optimum.
Calculate a **rate** from a change and a time.

The equation early and the graph late. Marks are point-for-point: one for the reading, one for the change, one for the division; and on a describe-and-explain pair, one for the trend **with a number from the graph** and one for the reason in terms of photosynthesis. Stuck: quote a number off the graph in every describe answer.
